'''Adam Leibovich''' (born March 23, 1970) is an American theoretical physicist. He is a full professor and the Bettye J. and Ralph E. Bailey Dean of the Kenneth P. Dietrich School of Arts and Sciences and the College of General Studies at the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. His research is primarily in [[quantum chromodynamics]] (QCD) and the application of [[effective field theory]] to problems of [[hadron]]ic physics, particularly particles containing one or more heavy [[quark]]s. Leibovich also has worked on gravitational wave physics. He was elected a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2017 and a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2018.

==Early life and education==
Leibovich is the son of [[Sidney Leibovich]], the Samuel B. Eckert Professor of Mechanical Engineering Emeritus at [[Cornell University]].<ref name="Cornell bio">{{cite web|title=Sidney Leibovich|url=https://www.duffield.cornell.edu/people/sidney-leibovich/|url-status=live|access-date=October 4, 2021|website=[[Cornell University]]|archive-date=October 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211003220911/https://www.mae.cornell.edu/faculty-directory/sidney-leibovich}}</ref> Adam Leibovich graduated from [[Cornell University]] with his [[Bachelor of Arts]] in physics, magma cum laude with honors, and attended the [[California Institute of Technology]] for his [[Ph.D.]] After completing his doctoral degree in 1997, he accepted postdoctoral positions at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] and [[Fermilab]].<ref name = "Pitt bio">{{cite web |title=Adam Leibovich |url=https://www.as.pitt.edu/adam-leibovich |website=[[University of Pittsburgh]] |accessdate=September 22, 2021 |archive-date=October 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211003220928/https://www.as.pitt.edu/adam-leibovich |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Career==
Leibovich joined the [[University of Pittsburgh]]'s (Pitt) Department of Physics and Astronomy as an [[assistant professor]] of physics in 2003. His research at Pitt focuses on [[QCD]], heavy [[quark]] physics, and [[gravitational wave]] physics. As a result of his research, he received an NSF CAREER award in 2006.<ref name = "career">{{cite press release |title=Three Pitt 'teacher-scholars' honored by NSF with CAREER awards |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/684179 |website=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science|Eurekalert]]|accessdate=September 22, 2021 |date=February 7, 2006 |archive-date=October 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211003220909/https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/684179 |url-status=live }}</ref> A popular instructor, Leibovich has also won teaching awards, including a 2006 Cottrell Scholar from the [[Research Corporation]] for Science Advancement <ref name="Pitt awards">{{cite web|title=Physics and Astronomy Faculty and Staff Awards|url=https://www.physicsandastronomy.pitt.edu/people/faculty-staff-awards|website=[[University of Pittsburgh]]|accessdate=September 22, 2021|date=June 15, 2006|archive-date=July 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210712211712/https://www.physicsandastronomy.pitt.edu/people/faculty-staff-awards|url-status=live}}</ref> and the Tina and David Bellet Teaching Award from the [[Dietrich School of Arts and Sciences]] at Pitt in 2010.<ref name = "DSAS awards">{{cite web|title=Dietrich School of Arts and Sciences Awards|url=https://www.as.pitt.edu/faculty/awards|website=[[University of Pittsburgh]]|accessdate=September 22, 2021|date=June 15, 2010|archive-date=October 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211003221031/https://www.as.pitt.edu/faculty/awards|url-status=live}}</ref>  Leibovich was named a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=December 2017|title=APS News, Vol. 26, No. 11|url=https://aps.org/publications/apsnews/201712/upload/December2017-rev.pdf|url-status=live|access-date=October 4, 2021|website=[[American Physical Society]]|archive-date=August 20, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200820002739/https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/201712/upload/December2017-rev.pdf}}</ref> in 2017 and a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Elected Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing|access-date=2021-10-04|website=[[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|language=en|archive-date=2018-10-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181007145732/https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing|url-status=live}}</ref> in 2018.

Leibovich was promoted to [[associate professor]] with tenure in 2008 and [[full professor]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Adam K Leibovich {{!}} Physics & Astronomy {{!}}|url=https://www.physicsandastronomy.pitt.edu/people/adam-k-leibovich|access-date=2021-10-04|website=[[University of Pittsburgh]]|archive-date=2021-10-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211003220930/https://www.physicsandastronomy.pitt.edu/people/adam-k-leibovich|url-status=live}}</ref> in 2015. He has held a variety of administrative rules during his time at Pitt, including Chair of Physics and Astronomy from 2015 to 2017, associate dean for Faculty Recruitment and Research Development from 2017 to 2021, and the associate dean for Research and Faculty Development.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Leibovich, Associate Dean for Research and Faculty Development {{!}} Kenneth P. Dietrich School of Arts & Sciences {{!}} University of Pittsburgh |url=https://www.as.pitt.edu/adam-leibovich-associate-dean-research-and-faculty-development |access-date=2023-05-04 |website=www.as.pitt.edu}}</ref> from 2021 to 2023 in the [[Dietrich School of Arts and Sciences]] where he oversaw research in the School, faculty hiring, and some budgetary issues, among other items.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dean's Office Organizational Chart|url=https://www.as.pitt.edu/sites/default/files/Dean%27s%20Office%20Chart%209.23.20.docx|url-status=live|access-date=October 5, 2021|website=[[University of Pittsburgh]]|archive-date=October 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211003222829/https://www.as.pitt.edu/sites/default/files/Dean%27s%20Office%20Chart%209.23.20.docx}}</ref> He was  the director of the [[Pittsburgh Quantum Institute]] from 2022 to 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dietrich School Associate Dean Named Director of Pittsburgh Quantum Institute |url=https://www.as.pitt.edu/news/dietrich-school-associate-dean-named-director-pittsburgh-quantum-institute |access-date=December 7, 2022}}</ref> On July 1, 2023, Leibovich started as the Dean of the [[Kenneth P. Dietrich School of Arts and Sciences]] and the [[University of Pittsburgh College of General Studies|College of General Studies]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adam Leibovich, Dean {{!}} Kenneth P. Dietrich School of Arts & Sciences {{!}} University of Pittsburgh |url=https://www.as.pitt.edu/adam-leibovich-dean |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=www.as.pitt.edu}}</ref>
